question: What dropout rate did the base Transformer use, and at which points in the network was dropout applied?
answer: The base Transformer uses a dropout rate of Pdrop = 0.1 [Attention Is All You Need, arXiv:1706.03762v7, pp. 7-8, Section 5.4 Regularization]. Dropout is applied to the output of each sub‑layer before it is added to the sub‑layer input and normalized [Attention Is All You Need, arXiv:1706.03762v7, pp. 7-8, Section 5.4 Regularization]. Dropout is also applied to the sums of the token embeddings and the positional encodings in both the encoder and decoder stacks [Attention Is All You Need, arXiv:1706.03762v7, pp. 7-8, Section 5.4 Regularization].
answer_raw: The base Transformer uses a dropout rate of Pdrop = 0.1 [P1]. Dropout is applied to the output of each sub‑layer before it is added to the sub‑layer input and normalized [P1]. Dropout is also applied to the sums of the token embeddings and the positional encodings in both the encoder and decoder stacks [P1].

question: Why does scaled dot-product attention divide the dot products by the square root of d_k?
answer: Scaled dot‑product attention divides the dot products by √d_k to prevent the dot products from becoming large in magnitude, which would push the softmax into regions with extremely small gradients; the scaling counteracts this effect [Attention Is All You Need, arXiv:1706.03762v7, p. 4, Section 3.2.1 Scaled Dot-Product Attention].
